NO CLINICAL OR OFFICIAL OUTBREAK ALERTS
How are seasonal patterns and unusual increases calculated?

Each baseline is the arithmetic mean of the same calendar month in all earlier years, using only months with a valid daily report for every calendar day. Flagging requires at least 3 such historical values and a complete current month. The highest baseline is called the historical peak only if all 12 months meet the history requirement. No future data is used. Thresholds are exploratory and not clinically validated. The optional trailing average requires 3 consecutive complete months.

What happens to missing, duplicate or partial reports?

Identical daily duplicates are counted once. If duplicate values conflict, that region/day is excluded. Monthly totals show only valid observed days. Every partial month is marked ◇ and is excluded from baseline and flag calculations. BBMP is kept separate from the Bengaluru Urban reporting series. A full set of report dates does not establish that every case was reported.

Does “check source” provide real-time dengue cases?

No. It downloads the publisher’s current CSV directly and compares its reporting cutoff with the bundled snapshot. It shows when the check succeeded and the latest date present. If the request fails, the existing data remains visible with a failure message. The source currently contains historical data; a successful connection does not mean the reports are current. No weather data is substituted for case data.

Can I import my own data?

CSV columns: date (YYYY-MM), region, cases, days, population (optional). Days is the count of valid daily reports in that month. Blank cases means missing; zero means observed zero. If days is missing, completeness is unknown and the month is not eligible for signals. Import replaces the explorer data in browser memory only. All files stay in your browser. Duplicate months and negative counts are rejected. Maximum file size: 2 MB.

THE PRESENTATION / 90 SECONDS

Show the evidence.
Then show your judgment.

  1. Start with real data. Show the source cutoff and explain that connected does not mean current.
  2. Scroll the history. Watch BBMP’s chart change across 2019, 2022 and 2024.
  3. Inspect a partial month. Tap a diamond point. Explain why it is excluded from signal assessment.
  4. Switch to Sample scenarios. Demonstrate the deliberate September spike and change the multiplier to 3×.
  5. Choose Mysuru, then Kodagu. Show missing data and insufficient history. These scenarios are synthetic and clearly labelled.

“DengueScope makes both the pattern and the quality of its evidence visible.”
